blocks.overview: This case concerns a cost assessment dispute between Penner (applicant) and Canada (respondent) following a prior court decision. The applicant claims costs have been extinguished by payment, which the respondent disputes. The Federal Court allowed 8 units of costs with adjustments, rejecting the applicant's extinguishment argument.

blocks.issue: What is the impact of the absence of opposition on the cost assessment and the role of the assessment officer?
blocks.court_conclusion: Assessment officer cannot certify unlawful items; assessment proceeds as parties have not settled; Defendant entitled to assessment.

positions.text: Does not dispute cost amount but asserts costs have been extinguished.
Argues no payment received; letter and bill of exchange do not amount to payment.
Assessment officer ensures compliance with judgment and rules; role does not include receiving payment; assessment proceeds.

blocks.issue: Are the units claimed in the Bill of Costs allowable and compliant with the Judgment and Rules?
blocks.court_conclusion: 8 units allowed with adjustments; 2 units reallocated; additional unit under Item 27 denied to avoid double indemnification.

positions.text: Claims 8 units per Column III, low end; supports attendance and preparation costs; requests additional unit under Item 27.
Allows units with adjustments to comply with Judgment; reallocates units; denies additional unit under Item 27; prevents double indemnification.

propositions.text: Defendant served and filed Bill of Costs, affidavit, and written submissions on December 3, 2024, initiating cost assessment

paragraphs.summary: The Defendant filed a Bill of Costs, affidavit, and submissions on December 3, 2024, starting the cost assessment.

propositions.text: Documents returned to Plaintiff by Registry on January 7, 2025, as payment into Court of costs claimed by Defendant without Court ruling or statutory provision
Issued first Direction on January 8, 2025, about conduct and filing of documents for cost assessment

paragraphs.summary: Registry returned documents to Plaintiff as payment on January 7, 2025; court issued Direction on January 8, 2025, about filing conduct.

propositions.text: Court Direction (Battista J.) on January 10, 2025, confirmed cost assessment proceeds under section 406 of Federal Courts Rules
Further Direction issued January 14, 2025, restating timelines for filing costs materials
Defendant reasserted request for cost assessment on January 14, 2025

paragraphs.summary: Court confirmed cost assessment under Rules on January 10, issued further Direction on January 14, Defendant reasserted request same day.

propositions.text: Plaintiff submitted unserved materials dated January 25, 2025, to Registry on February 6, 2025
Direction on February 12, 2025, accepted Plaintiff's materials except five pages with unclear public status financial info
Five pages sent to Defendant as attachment; Plaintiff advised to resubmit suitable for public viewing

paragraphs.summary: Plaintiff submitted unserved materials on February 6, 2025; court accepted them except five financial pages, sent to Defendant, advised Plaintiff to resubmit.

propositions.text: Direction of February 12 extended timelines due to Plaintiff's non-adherence to filing sequence
Direction clarified if Plaintiff consents to payment, it must be paid directly to Defendant, not Registry or Court
Assessment of costs would proceed unless parties settled and request discontinued

paragraphs.summary: Court extended timelines on February 12, clarified payment must go directly to Defendant if consented, and assessment proceeds unless settled.

propositions.text: Defendant did not file additional materials after February 12 Direction
Plaintiff filed supplemental materials on March 31, 2025, indicating documents considered as payment delivered to Defendant
Supplemental materials unserved; attached to July 8, 2025 Direction allocating time for Defendant's reply

paragraphs.summary: Defendant filed no new materials after February 12; Plaintiff filed supplemental materials March 31; court attached them to July 8 Direction for Defendant's reply.

propositions.text: Defendant served and filed reply on July 24, 2025, confirming assessment still required and no effective payment made

paragraphs.summary: Defendant replied on July 24, 2025, confirming assessment needed and no effective payment made.

propositions.text: Plaintiff's short letter with questions placed in Court record on July 16, 2025, not submitted per timelines or served on Defendant
Letter will not be considered as it lacks submissions or evidence
Considering letter would not change assessment outcome

paragraphs.summary: Plaintiff's July 16 letter with questions not timely submitted or served; court will not consider it and says it would not affect outcome.

propositions.text: Preliminary issues: impact of absence of opposition on assessment and role of assessment officer

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies preliminary issues: absence of opposition impact and assessment officer's role.

propositions.text: Plaintiff does not dispute cost amount or content but asserts costs have been extinguished

paragraphs.summary: Plaintiff does not dispute cost amount but claims costs have been extinguished.

propositions.text: Without substantive opposition, assessment officer cannot certify unlawful items outside judgment and Tariff (Dahl v Canada)
Assessment officer not bound by consent to costs for items not complying with legal framework
Assessment officer will ensure claimed services comply with Judgment, procedural steps, Rules, and jurisprudence

paragraphs.summary: Court states assessment officer cannot certify unlawful items and must ensure claimed services comply with law despite no opposition.

propositions.text: Defendant argues it did not receive payment; letter and bill of exchange do not amount to payment
Defendant notes bill of exchange similar to one in Plaintiff's struck Statement of Claim was sent

paragraphs.summary: Defendant argues no payment received; letter and bill of exchange insufficient; bill similar to one in struck claim was sent.

propositions.text: Plaintiff disagrees with Defendant's position that costs have not been extinguished

paragraphs.summary: Plaintiff disagrees that costs have not been extinguished.

propositions.text: Plaintiff's documents refer to bill of exchange tendered as payment of $1,440 costs claimed
Plaintiff's documents mention remittance sent to set off and discharge amount stated on Defendant's Bill of Costs
Plaintiff alleges payment delivered by sending bill on March 24, 2025, and refusal to receive payment under protest loses right of recourse

paragraphs.summary: Plaintiff's documents claim bill of exchange and remittance sent as payment and allege refusal to accept payment loses recourse rights.

propositions.text: Assessment of costs purpose is not to determine validity of payment method or extinguishment of costs
Assessment officer role does not include receiving payment unless Court instructs, which is not the case

paragraphs.summary: Court states assessment officer does not determine payment validity or receive payment unless Court instructs, which did not occur.

propositions.text: Assessment officers are Registry officers appointed by Court; Court consists of judges under Federal Courts Act
Assessment officer's jurisdiction is to establish quantum of costs awarded by Court (Rule 405; Pelletier v Canada)

paragraphs.summary: Court explains assessment officers are Registry officers with jurisdiction to establish cost quantum awarded by Court.

propositions.text: Defendant contends Plaintiff's actions during assessment were improper
Court did not consider Defendant's argument about validity of Plaintiff's documents as outside assessment officer's jurisdiction

paragraphs.summary: Defendant alleges Plaintiff acted improperly; court did not consider this as outside assessment officer's jurisdiction.

propositions.text: Parties have not settled; request for assessment maintained; Defendant entitled to assessment to establish costs payable by Plaintiff

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no settlement; Defendant entitled to cost assessment to establish amount payable by Plaintiff.

propositions.text: Defendant claims 8 units for assessable services totaling $1,440; no disbursements claimed
Plaintiff did not substantially oppose Bill of Costs content

paragraphs.summary: Defendant claims 8 units totaling $1,440; Plaintiff did not substantially oppose the Bill of Costs.

propositions.text: Defendant submits Bill of Costs prepared per Column III of Rule 407, intending low end of range, though units differ for some items

paragraphs.summary: Defendant submits Bill of Costs prepared per Rule 407 Column III, intending low end, though units differ for some items.

propositions.text: 8 units claimed in the Bill of Costs will be allowed with some adjustments to comply with the Judgment

paragraphs.summary: The court allows 8 units claimed in the Bill of Costs with some adjustments to comply with the Judgment.

propositions.text: The single unit under Item 25 for 'Services after judgment not otherwise specified' is allowed as submitted
Item 25 is routinely permitted to cover counsel’s review of the final decision concluding the file (Halford v Seed Hawk Inc)
The single unit claimed under Item 6 for Defendant’s attendance at the hearing to strike is allowed as submitted
Defendant’s submissions and evidence support the claim for attendance at the hearing (Defendant’s Written Submissions, paras 1 and 3; Affidavit of Jessica Vallatti, para 2)

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the single units claimed under Items 25 and 6 are allowed as submitted, supported by Defendant’s submissions and Halford precedent.

propositions.text: 5 units are claimed under Item 5 for preparing and filing the Motion to Strike the Statement of Claim
Defendant’s costs materials state intent to formulate claims based on the low end of Column III

paragraphs.summary: The court notes 5 units claimed under Item 5, but Defendant intended claims based on the low end of Column III.

propositions.text: Claim under Item 26 is 1 unit below the minimum under Column III warranted by the Judgment
Assessment officer cannot go beyond or contradict the judge’s order (Pelletier at para 7)
Assessment officer cannot depart from Column III or change minimum allowable amount (Interactive Sports Technologies Inc v Canada)
Rule 3 will be applied to resolve the discrepancy regarding Item 26

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Item 26 claim below minimum; assessment officer cannot contradict judge’s order; Rule 3 will resolve the discrepancy.

propositions.text: Rule 3 requires Rules be interpreted to secure just, expeditious, and least expensive outcomes

paragraphs.summary: Rule 3 requires interpreting Rules to secure just, expeditious, and least expensive outcomes.

propositions.text: Assessment Officer in Mitchell v Canada emphasized positive application of provisions to achieve equitable results on assessment

paragraphs.summary: The Assessment Officer in Mitchell emphasized positive application of provisions for equitable assessment results.

propositions.text: 2 units claimed under Item 5 will be subtracted and reallocated to Item 26 to comply with Judgment and secure just outcome

paragraphs.summary: The court reallocates 2 units from Item 5 to Item 26 to comply with Judgment and ensure just outcome.

propositions.text: After subtracting 2 units, 3 units are allowed under Item 5

paragraphs.summary: The court allows 3 units under Item 5 after subtracting 2 units.

propositions.text: Defendant claims 1 unit under Item 26 for work on assessment of costs, below minimum under Column III
An error appears to have been made in preparing Bill of Costs for Item 26

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Defendant claims 1 unit under Item 26, below minimum, likely due to error in Bill of Costs preparation.

propositions.text: Rule 408(3) allows assessment officer to assess and allow or refuse costs of assessment
Defendant prepared comprehensive costs materials and increased Directions required effort
Units should be allowed for work performed on this assessment, but single unit claimed does not comply with Judgment

paragraphs.summary: The court finds units should be allowed for assessment work, but single unit claimed does not comply with Judgment.

propositions.text: Carlile decision states taxing at zero dollars is improper alternative to full amount

paragraphs.summary: Carlile decision states taxing at zero dollars is improper alternative to full amount.

propositions.text: Correcting units claimed for Item 26 is appropriate to comply with Judgment, adding 2 units to claimed 1 unit for total 3 units
3 units allowed fall within lower end of Column III and align with Defendant’s intended claim and Rule 400(3) factors

paragraphs.summary: The court corrects Item 26 units to 3, within Column III and aligned with Defendant’s intent and Rule 400(3) factors.

propositions.text: Court concluded Plaintiff may be engaging in vexatious and abusive conduct (Defendant’s Reply, p 1)
Considered result of proceeding and amount of work by Defendant in allowing 3 units under Item 26 per Rule 400(3)(a) and (g)

paragraphs.summary: The court considered Plaintiff’s vexatious conduct and Defendant’s work amount in allowing 3 units under Item 26.

propositions.text: Defendant requests additional unit under Item 27 due to Plaintiff’s improper payment delays and waste of court time
This additional unit under Item 27 will not be allowed

paragraphs.summary: The Defendant requests an additional unit under Item 27 for Plaintiff’s improper conduct; the court denies this request.

propositions.text: Claim under Item 27 must be included in Bill of Costs or revised Bill per Tariff B and Rule 406
No unit would be allowed under Item 27 based on submissions even if claim included

paragraphs.summary: The court rules Item 27 claims must be in Bill of Costs; no unit would be allowed even if included.

propositions.text: Defendant says Item 27 indemnifies counsel for extraordinary items not covered elsewhere in Tariff
Item 27 compensates for assessable services by counsel, not work by assessment officer or judicial resources

paragraphs.summary: Defendant says Item 27 covers extraordinary items; court rules it compensates counsel’s assessable services, not assessment officer’s work.

propositions.text: Compensation for work on assessment should be claimed under Item 26, not Item 27

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes work on assessment should be claimed under Item 26, not Item 27.

propositions.text: Item 27 applies only for services not addressed by Items 1 to 26 (Halford at para 131)
Defendant already compensated with 3 units under Item 26; allowing additional unit under Item 27 would be double indemnification
Double indemnification is not permitted

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Item 27 applies only to services not covered by Items 1-26; Defendant already compensated under Item 26; double indemnification disallowed.

propositions.text: 8 units are allowed for assessable services, totaling $1,440

paragraphs.summary: The court allows 8 units for assessable services totaling $1,440.
